security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown false positives, not executable shell constructs. Confirmed risks remain from external network calls, private-key environment access, .env.local modification, subprocess guidance, mutable remote refetching, and on-chain write operations.

remediation.issue: On-chain writes can deploy or resolve contracts without an explicit safety checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user approval immediately before every writeContract call, deployment shortcut, or resolve call.

remediation.issue: The skill can refetch mutable remote instructions from intelligentoracle.com.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the self-refetch instruction or require pinned hashes for any remote skill content.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples read PRIVATE_KEY and RPC_URL values from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer ephemeral Studionet accounts by default and require explicit opt-in before reading any private key.

remediation.issue: The raw RPC section recommends shelling out to a Node subprocess.
remediation.suggestion: Replace subprocess guidance with a reviewed helper path and fixed arguments that never include unsanitized user input.

remediation.issue: The deploy shortcut writes configuration to .env.local.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact file changes and require user confirmation before running commands that modify environment files.

content.value_statement: Creating an oracle market requires strict fields, source rules, and contract calls. This skill drafts, deploys, verifies, and monitors GenLayer Intelligent Oracle markets.
actual_capabilities: Drafts binary prediction market configurations with two outcomes.
Validates required oracle fields and source-domain rules.
Fetches the current factory pointer and RPC endpoint guidance.
Shows how to deploy a market with genlayer-js.
Verifies deployed oracle fields after creation.
Monitors oracle status and explains resolution states.
limitations: Markets must resolve to exactly two outcomes.
Resolution depends on public web evidence and validator consensus.
Deployment requires network access and may require a wallet or key.
The skill cannot guarantee the final oracle outcome.

use_cases.title: Launch a Market Draft
use_cases.description: Create a valid Yes or No market configuration from a plain-language event idea.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Test Oracle
use_cases.description: Use Studionet deployment steps to create and verify a GenLayer oracle contract.

use_cases.title: Monitor Resolution Status
use_cases.description: Check an oracle after launch and understand whether it is active, resolved, or in error.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Yes or No oracle market about [event]. Use a reliable public source and choose a future resolution date.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Market Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Tighten the resolution rules for this market: [market summary]. Keep exactly two outcomes and explain the source choice.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this oracle market for deployment readiness. Check fields, source domains, and the earliest resolution date.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor and Resolve
prompt_templates.prompt: Given oracle address [address], outline the checks to verify deployment, monitor status, and trigger resolution after the eligible date.

output_examples.input: Will Bitcoin close above a chosen price at the end of 2026?
output_examples.output: A concise market title, a Yes or No outcome set, Binance as the price source, and a resolution date after the event.

output_examples.input: Check whether my deployed oracle is finished.
output_examples.output: A status-focused response that explains whether the oracle is active, resolved, or in error, with the key address and title.

output_examples.input: Create a sports market for a future championship result.
output_examples.output: A binary market draft using a sports source, clear winner rules, and a resolution date after the final match.

best_practices: Confirm every deployment or resolution write before executing it.
Use fixed URLs only when the user provides stable pages.
Log only transaction hashes, oracle addresses, and essential state fields.
anti_patterns: Do not create markets with more than two possible outcomes.
Do not mix resolution URLs and source domains in one config.
Do not read private keys unless the user explicitly approves.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates GenLayer Intelligent Oracle prediction market drafts and deployment workflows.

faq.question: Does it require funded keys?
faq.answer: The skill defaults to Studionet, which is described as free for testing.

faq.question: Can it support three or more outcomes?
faq.answer: No. The documented oracle configuration requires exactly two distinct outcomes.

faq.question: Can it use any website as evidence?
faq.answer: It prefers verified source domains and can use fixed URLs when the user provides them.

faq.question: Does it automatically resolve markets?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains that a resolve call must be made after the earliest resolution date.

faq.question: What should users approve carefully?
faq.answer: Users should approve network calls, private-key use, contract deployment, resolution calls, and environment file changes.
